result.summary: This fan-animated nature documentary depicts the leisurely lifestyle and behavior of Torterra in a lush forest and meadow environment. A male Torterra wakes up, slowly treks to a lake for water, briefly attempts to pursue a female mate, and quickly returns to resting.

transcript.text: For the Torterra, life is best enjoyed in the slow lane.
They spend the bulk of their days napping, and not much else.
Conserving precious energy is a time-tested strategy in an otherwise fast-paced world.
But resting in one spot loses its charm after a while.
It's about time for a change of pace.
Rarely seen in motion, groups of Torterra are often mistaken for moving forests.
This male seems a bit too fond of his lounging spot to join the others.
Though a drink of water would be nice.
There should be a lake just beyond the trees.
It's not too far. He'll get there... eventually.
Of course, a sudden surge of movement from a Torterra can spell trouble for those living on his back.
For some unlucky residents, it will take some work to get back home.
For everyone else, it's going to be a bumpy ride.
Within the next few hours or so, this determined Torterra will finally arrive at his destination.
He's almost there.
Fresh water at last.
But he's not the only one in search of a refreshment.
A female approaches.
Sensing a potential mate, he springs to life with a burst of agility and sets off in hot pursuit.
Sadly, the lady Torterra doesn't seem very interested.
And giving chase is too much work for our lounge-loving male.
He may have failed this time, but he's more than happy to enjoy another rest.
After all, there's no reason to rush.
Perhaps slow and steady will someday work in his favor.

observations.text: An aerial view displays several Torterra resting motionless in a sunny meadow surrounded by trees.
Close-up ground view of Torterra sleeping flat on the grass.
Three Morelull walk across the grass past the sleeping Torterra's snout as it blinks awake.
A Combee flies near the head of a slumbering Torterra, hovering in front of its nose.
The Torterra opens its eyes and mouth, disturbed by the Combee.
A high-angle shot reveals multiple Torterra walking forward together across the clearing.
Wide scenic shot overlooking a vast green forest canopy illuminated by morning sunlight.
A lone Torterra remains resting while the rest of the herd walks away into the distance.
Close-up of the lazy male Torterra resting on the grass and yawning.
View across a forest clearing toward a calm lake surrounded by trees.
The male Torterra slowly lifts itself up and begins a slow walk toward the lake.
A Zigzagoon clinging to the tree on Torterra's shell loses its footing and tumbles off onto the grass.
Three Morelull hold on tightly atop the rock spikes of the Torterra's moving shell.
The Torterra crawls forward across a meadow dotted with orange wildflowers.
The Torterra reaches the grassy water's edge and lowers its head toward the lake surface.
A female Torterra appears walking across the meadow in the background.
The male turns sharply and accelerates into a quick jog toward the female.
The female Torterra ignores him and continues walking away into the distance.
The male stops chasing, rests his head against the grass, and settles down to sleep again.
Wide panoramic shot showing the resting Torterra alone on the lake shore.
Patreon patron credits scroll over behind-the-scenes 3D clay render passes of the animation.

A three-celled honey bee Pokémon flies around Torterra's snout and over flowers.
A small striped raccoon-like Pokémon falls off the tree on Torterra's shell.

lore.subject: Torterra
lore.fact: Groups of migrating Torterra are frequently mistaken for moving forests, and smaller Pokémon often live their entire lives on a Torterra's shell.
